summary: Doug Smith and Broderbund's Lode Runner is a landmark puzzle-platform game with early level-editor importance, later remade and ported many times across computers, consoles, and modern storefronts.

entries.title: Lode Runner
entries.definitive_edition: Original 1983 Apple II/microcomputer release, with platform and level-editor state documented

emulation.emulator: Apple II / C64 / PC booter emulator depending on chosen original platform
emulation.notes: Prefer the Apple II route for the origin baseline; record emulator, disk image provenance, and timing settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original microcomputer behavior with exact platform documented

primary.why: The Apple II and contemporary microcomputer versions preserve the original 150-level puzzle-platform design and built-in editor. Modern Lode Runner Legacy is an official new entry/remake route, but it is not a substitute for the 1983 game.
primary.how_to_play: Use original Apple II hardware or accurate Apple II emulation from a legitimately sourced copy. Record platform, disk/version, controller/keyboard setup, level number, editor-created level use, speed/timing settings, and whether later NES/arcade or Legacy routes were compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Modern official voxel remake/entry with sharing and editors
secondary.what_to_play: Use only as a modern comparison route.
secondary.why: It is currently accessible and official, but it changes presentation and is not the original 1983 archive target.

secondary.platform: Famicom / NES / arcade and other ports
secondary.exclusive_content: Port-specific level sets, scrolling, music, and presentation changes
secondary.why: The microcomputer original is the fidelity baseline.

entries.remaster_caveats: Lode Runner Legacy and later console/arcade ports should be labeled as comparison routes, not replacements for the original.
